clue.text: Interpret two bits of text

parts.note: the first of two bits is a PARA, short for paragraph, a section of writing
the second bit of text is a phrase, a short group of words

explanation.surface: An instruction to make sense of a couple of short passages of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two bits of text' is shared between both pieces: a paragraph (PARA) and a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate a passage in other words, a way of interpreting it.

clue.text: Oppose petition, swapping sides

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so the R in the word is exchanged for an L

parts.note: to petition is to pray, ask earnestly

explanation.surface: Someone argues against a petition by switching allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in PRAY becomes L (left), the 'sides' being swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport you play a team when you oppose it in a match.

clue.text: Nuclear plants lacking atomic mass conductors?

indicators.note: lacking says a piece is dropped from the word for nuclear plants

parts.note: the cores of nuclear power stations are reactors
A is the symbol for mass number, the atomic mass of a nucleus

explanation.surface: Power stations missing something in their physics are poor conductors of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'conductors' means people who conduct church services, not electrical conductors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectors are parish clergy, who lead or conduct services in their churches.

clue.text: Trick from a card you'd rather not be dealt?

definitions.text: Trick from a card you'd rather not be dealt?

parts.words: Trick from a card you'd rather not be dealt?
parts.note: a prank played by a joker, a person who is a 'card', that you would prefer not to receive, with a nod to the joker in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card game where an unwanted card turns up in your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'card' is also a jokey person; what such a person deals out is a prank, and the joker card lurks in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank involving physical action rather than words is a trick of this kind, often unwelcome to its victim.

clue.text: On and coming up, kind of movie guide

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for the movie is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an epic is a grand, sweeping kind of film

explanation.surface: A film genre on the rise gets a guide to watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions that guides a cook through a dish.

clue.text: Working as lecturer, perhaps, son going to a summit

parts.note: peaking means reaching a peak or summit

explanation.surface: A lecturer's son is off climbing mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer works by giving talks, so delivering a lecture is a form of public address.

clue.text: Feeble learner, mischievous child

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a car
an imp is a little rascal

explanation.surface: A weak pupil who is also a little rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness or strength, as a feeble handshake does.

clue.text: Middle Easterner is famously mad ruler, twisted one

indicators.note: twisted says the king's name is turned round

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's king who goes mad
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern figure is called a crazed, warped tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel is a native of the Middle East.

clue.text: Upturn after papers united in force

indicators.note: after places the upturn following the papers and united

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
a rise is an upturn, an increase

explanation.surface: A rise in circulation after newspapers band together in strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressurise someone is to push or coerce them into doing something.

clue.text: Old-fashioned bridge clubs with interior first-rate

indicators.note: with interior says the first-rate piece sits inside the bridge-and-clubs combination

parts.note: an arch is a curved bridging structure
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
A1 (written AI) means first-rate

explanation.surface: Bridge clubs are dated places, though excellent inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge clubs' reads as card-game venues; 'bridge' is the structure and 'clubs' the card suit, and 'with interior' puts the first-rate piece between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic belongs to an earlier era, so it is out of date.

clue.text: Insist on piece of chicken for celebration

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone demands a portion of chicken at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took only 'Insist' as the definition; 'Insist on' is the phrase that swaps for ENFORCE, since 'enforce' takes an object just as 'insist on' does.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule is to insist on it being obeyed.

clue.text: Cat sat, finally tumbling in well

indicators.note: tumbling says the letters of the three words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat that eventually sat down, then tumbled into a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like a last-letter indicator but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastically is an intensified way of saying very well, as in getting on fantastically.

clue.text: Frank talking away, gave address west of Northern Cape

indicators.note: in an across clue, west of puts the preceding pieces to the left of the cape

parts.note: out means away, not at home
spoke means talked, gave an address
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A frank speaker went off and lectured somewhere west of the Northern Cape in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Cape is a South African province, but here it splits into N and NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspokenness is candour in speech, the quality of saying bluntly what you think.

clue.text: Extra seconds with last of soup dipped into — it's common!

parts.note: in cricket a wide is an extra, a run conceded for a ball bowled out of reach

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of soup

parts.note: to dip into a book is to read some of it

explanation.surface: Extra helpings of soup, with a final dip into the bowl, are found everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide in cricket is a ball bowled too far from the batter, giving the batting side a free run.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread is found in many places, so it is prevalent rather than rare.

clue.text: Annoying being part of cult?

parts.note: to be in something is to be part of it
a sect is a religious group or cult

explanation.surface: Someone irksome turns out to be a member of a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' looks like a hidden-word indicator, but the answer is not hidden in 'cult'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects such as flies and mosquitoes are creatures that pester people.

clue.text: Erase ink smudges, getting more shady

indicators.note: smudges says the letters of the two words are smeared into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbing out ink leaves blurred marks, looking ever more suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneakier is the comparative of sneaky, meaning more furtive or underhand.

clue.text: Witness seized by Ethelred — lo, he begs to get up

indicators.note: to get up says the hidden letters are read backwards
seized by says the letters are held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king pleads with a witness to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'seized' into the definition and gave the hidden word no indicator; 'seized by' is that indicator, and 'Witness' alone is the definition. Ethelred was an English king.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who sees or observes something, as an onlooker witnesses an event.

clue.text: Cheer is loud — two letters in a row written about it

indicators.note: written about it says the two spelt-out letters go round the word for loud

parts.note: M and N stand side by side in the alphabet; spelt out they are EM and EN
bold, like loud, describes a striking, showy colour or pattern

explanation.surface: A cheer is noisy, and someone spells out letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone in the sense of giving them heart is to make them braver.

clue.text: Mention turnover of local housing syndicate

indicators.note: housing says the reversed pub holds the syndicate inside it
turnover of says the word for local is turned back to front

parts.note: in Britain your local is your nearest pub
a ring is a group working together, a syndicate

explanation.surface: A financial report on a pub-owning syndicate's sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business takings but reverses PUB to BUP, which then houses RING.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a subject is to raise or mention it in conversation.

clue.text: SOS vet broadcast for cooking equipment

indicators.note: broadcast says the letters are scattered and re-sown in a new order

explanation.surface: A vet sends out a distress call about kitchen appliances.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoves are ranges or cookers, appliances for heating food.

clue.text: One's base: Roman building, all the rage

parts.note: a villa is a Roman country house
in means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: A Roman villa is someone's fashionable home base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' reads as a home or headquarters, but means morally low: a base one.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person, someone whose character is low and contemptible.

clue.text: Composer about to be supported by board

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to hop in is to board a vehicle

explanation.surface: A composer about to be propped up on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish Romantic composer of piano music.

clue.text: Having reformed a school, Philip resigned

indicators.note: reformed says the letters of the words are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Philip quit his post after overhauling a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Being philosophical about a setback means accepting it calmly, as someone resigned to it does.

clue.text: Look to go north or south

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether travelling up or down the grid

parts.note: a quick glance; the same word serves as the letters the palindrome reading tests

explanation.surface: A glance in either direction along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick, furtive glance.

clue.text: Breakfast food boss offers Einstein

parts.note: an egg is a breakfast staple
the head is the boss, the person in charge

explanation.surface: A manager serves breakfast to the great physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein stands for a genius, and an intellectual is informally called this.

clue.text: Loot not well concealed by sheet

indicators.note: concealed by says the word for unwell is tucked inside the word for sheet

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Stolen goods hidden under a bedsheet by someone off sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillage is to plunder or loot, especially in war.

clue.text: Trick of the French to forego training

indicators.note: forego means go before, so the French piece precedes the training

parts.note: du is French for of the
PE is physical education, school training

explanation.surface: A French person skipping their exercise class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forego' reads as 'do without', but here it is fore-go, to go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to deceive or fool them.

clue.text: It may cause scoffing and make Yankee shoot

parts.note: a make is a brand of goods
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to snap is to shoot a photograph

explanation.surface: Something provokes jeering and an American photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' means eating greedily, not mocking. A brandy snap is a crisp rolled British biscuit, often cream-filled.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a sweet treat that people gobble up, scoff being slang for eat greedily.
